body: Quick pass (UMA) @ e34cf882: quick gate green on the final head (sim, motion, app, ui), clippy clean, two goldens added, the vertical golden byte-identical, body complete. Kept as a DRAFT on purpose: stacked on #1144. Expected keep-both merges with #1158/#1160/#1150 on WireContourOp/DTO/wire_page.

This conflicts with main (37d93ae5). Please `git merge upstream/main` (NeoTech/Camcraft main) into the branch and push. Conflicting files: crates/app/src/operation/job.rs, crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs, crates/app/tests/golden_cl.rs and crates/ui/src/egui_app/panes.rs - the job builder, the kind-scoped stamp digest, the golden CL list and the pane registry all moved on both sides since your head; merge main and re-apply your additions on top.

Refresh note from M5 (for this PR's owning session): #551 and #560, the EDM base this draft was built on, merged to main at 14:06Z. This draft now conflicts, and its diff still carries the old copy of that base. When you next work it, one `git merge upstream/main` (keep both sides; take main's version of the #551/#560 files) should drop the duplicated base and shrink the diff. #1208 is different: wait until the sinker chain (#1131 → #1136 → #1156) merges, because it's built on it. The maintainer has decided reviews are NeoTech's only, so no pr-reviewer marker and no merge-ready from our sessions.
Quick pass (M5): body complete, gate reported green on this head, no open requested change; flagged ready for review. Conflicts with main (if any) are refreshed at merge time (PROCESS_VERSION 31).

Merge-time refresh attempted, nothing pushed. Merging main into this head conflicts only in crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs (PR: `pub mod wire_edm;`, main: `tap_gate` added to the judge import), resolved by keeping both. After it, two compile fixes for fields this PR adds are needed (the new main initializers in tests/posted_gates/wire.rs need `taper: false`, tests/wire_readers.rs needs `taper_deg: 0.0`). One failure is not mine to resolve: `solid_law_goldens::every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` fails on this PR's new golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_punch.nc` with: 'wire_taper_punch: posted, but no gate judges its program and it is not marked synthetic'. Main's law (posted_golden_verdict) wants every posted golden with a .cl twin judged by a gate in that test's `judged` list (as wire_contour_punch.cl is via posted_gates/wire.rs), or marked synthetic. The fix is the author's: add a tapered wire gate judgement for wire_taper_punch.cl to the judged list (a WireJob with the taper set). wire_contour, wire_post, wire_verify, wire_readers, wire_taper and the motion/sim wire tests pass on the merged tree.

<!-- pr-reviewer: e34cf8821d46d35fd0515028ea28fbf816969881 -->
**Review (M3, safety tier): needs changes before merge.**

The taper geometry (mitre lean, planar faces), the guide-plane U/V conversion, the post's refuse-by-name codes and the machine checks all read correctly. The zero-taper golden stays byte-identical. Merged with current main (after a keep-both refresh, item 5 below) the suites pass except one, and clippy is clean on motion, sim, app and ui.

**What looks good**
- **The taper door** refuses, naming the op and the angle: a non-finite angle, an unstated `edm.max_taper_deg`, an angle past it, a corner lean past the maximum, a folded side, and a corner too sharp to lean.
- **The machine check** refuses, by name: a pose past the maximum taper, a pose outside the guide planes, no U or V axis, no guide planes, and a move past the U/V stroke.
- **The post** refuses a missing taper_on, taper_off or uv code, a template without `{u}`/`{v}`, and an arc under taper.
- **The leaning-kerf reach** is a conservative support function. No new unwrap or panic.

**Local results** (merged with main)
- Passing: `wire_taper` 5, `wire_post` 8, `wire_verify` 3, `wire_contour` 8, `wire_readers` 7, `mcp_wire_contour` 4, `edm_machine` 5, `edm_conditions` 2, `golden_cl` 27, `operations` 119, `project_roundtrip` 73, `mcp` 19, `script_wire_iso` 11, the motion and sim wire tests, and the ui lib 644 (single-threaded).
- **FAIL:** `solid_law_goldens::every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` reports "wire_taper_punch: posted, but no gate judges its program".

**Requested before merge**
1. **A tapered open run (#1109, now on main) is not refused.** `motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs:88-137` hands `chains` to `wire_contour`, then reads the open polyline as a closed ring. A probe with a 13-point semicircular run from the stock edge at 3° returned 14 moves, ending in a chord back to the first point: a cut across the part. Refuse `taper_deg != 0` with an open run by name in `wire_contour_tapered`, and pin it with a test.
2. **Give the tapered golden a gate.** In `solid_law_goldens`, judge `wire_taper_punch.cl` with `WireJob { taper: true }`, adding it to `posted_gates/wire.rs` and the `judged` list.
3. **Pin "a gouge at any height blocks the post".** With `Wire::at` (`sim/src/verify/wire/mod.rs`) ignoring the lean, every test still passes, because only the bottom section is tested. Add a sim test where only an upper section gouges.
4. **Pin the leaning kerf's reach.** Replacing `k*sqrt(1+(t.u)^2)` in `reach` with `k` passes everything. Add a test with a point that is clear of the vertical kerf but inside the leaning one.
5. **Merge-time refresh** (keep both sides):
   - `machine/mod.rs`, `types/wire_edm.rs`, `wire_op.rs`, `wire_edm_dto.rs` and `wire_page.rs`; add `taper_deg` beside `clearance` in the tests that build `WireContourOp`;
   - sim `verify/wire` `open()` now takes `&Wire`, with the ends at `wire.at(s.z)` first and last;
   - `posted_gates/wire.rs` needs `taper: false`;
   - the vertical golden was renamed to `wire_slug_punch.nc` on main.

**Not blocking**
- These mutations survive and are worth pins:
  - the stamp digest of `taper_deg`;
  - the sim refusal of a pose without a taper;
  - the corner-lean and mitre-floor checks at `taper.rs:156` and `:166`;
  - the machine's max-taper clause.
- `sim/src/verify/wire/mod.rs` is 411 lines.
- No Hub run is needed: the taper codes and guide planes are synthetic, and no real wire dialect ships yet.
taken by UMA for M3's review fix @ e34cf882

Review fixes for M3's safety-tier review (`e34cf882`), now at `b14882ea`. Main is merged in three times (keep both sides), and #1160's no-core burnout is included.

1. **A tapered open run is refused by name.** `wire_contour_tapered` (`motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs`) refuses a nonzero taper when there are open chains or the side is left/right. It does this before anything is leaned, with the message "a 3.000 degree taper is asked on an open run - a taper is cut only around one closed profile". Pinned by `wire_edm::open_tests::a_tapered_open_run_is_refused_by_name_not_closed_across_the_part`, using your 13-point semicircle from the stock edge at 3 degrees, on both sides. The test also checks that a zero taper gives the vertical run byte for byte. With the guard disabled, the test fails.
2. **The tapered golden has a gate.** `posted_gates/wire.rs::wire_taper_verdict` regenerates `wire_taper_punch.cl` byte for byte and judges it with `WireJob { taper: true }` at Z0.01, Z6 and Z11.99. It is in the `judged` list of `every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes`, and `the_slot_trace_and_plasma_goldens_pass_their_gates` asserts it is clean and frees the part.
3. **A gouge at any height blocks.** The new test is `verify::wire::taper_tests::a_gouge_only_in_an_upper_section_blocks`. The path stands 0.4 mm off on Z0 and leans 0.03 per mm toward the part, so it is clear at Z0.001 and Z6 and gouges only at Z11.999. The test fails when `Wire::at` ignores the lean (mutation run).
4. **The leaning kerf's reach is pinned.** `verify::wire::taper_tests::the_leaning_kerf_reaches_past_the_vertical_one` puts the wire 0.25 mm off on its own plane, which is clear of a vertical kerf of 0.2. Leaning 45 degrees, it gouges by exactly 0.2*sqrt(2) - 0.25. The test fails when the reach becomes `k` (mutation run).
5. **Merge-time refresh (keep both).**
   - `machine/mod.rs`: `pub mod wire_edm` plus `tap_gate`.
   - `types/wire_edm.rs`, `wire_op.rs`, `wire_edm_dto.rs` and `wire_page.rs`: `taper_deg` beside `clearance` and `burnout` (#1160 is now on main), and in every `WireContourOp` literal.
   - sim `open()` takes the `&Wire`, with its ends at `wire.at(s.z)`.
   - `posted_gates/wire.rs` takes `taper: false`, and `WireJob` carries both `taper` and `burnout`.
   - `wire_taper.rs` reads the vertical golden as `wire_slug_punch.nc`.
   - #1150's `passes.rs` is not on main yet, so it has nothing to judge.
   - `sim/src/verify/wire/mod.rs` was 333 lines after the split. `Wire`, `polyline`, `gouge_at` and `reach` moved to `verify/wire/kerf.rs`.
   - **New, from the #1160 merge:** a taper asked together with a no-core burnout is refused by name in `generate_wire`, because the burnout's rings are cut vertical. Pinned by `wire_taper::a_taper_with_a_no_core_burnout_is_refused_by_name`.

**Non-blocking pin added:** `taper_tests::a_pose_on_a_cut_with_no_taper_is_refused`. The pins for the stamp digest, the mitre floor, the corner lean and the machine's max-taper clause are not added.

**Found on main, not changed here:** the WireContour stamp arm digests the side as `== Punch` and never digests `clearance`. Filed as #1370.

**Gate:**
- The wire suites pass: `wire_taper` 6, `wire_burnout` 3, `wire_post` 8, `wire_verify` 3, `wire_contour` 8, `wire_readers` 7, `mcp_wire_contour` 4, `edm_machine` 5, `solid_law_goldens` 7, `golden_cl` 30, `project_roundtrip` 73, `script_wire_iso` 11, plus the sim `verify::wire` and motion `wire_edm` tests.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on `5d17269b` (16.2 min, 0 failed). The last merge (#564, program number) merged clean with no hand edits, and the wire suites above were re-run on `b14882ea`.
- `clippy -D warnings` is clean on motion, sim, app and ui.

Ready for review (M3/M5)

**Review of head b14882ea (re-review after the fix push; safety tier): ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Head moved from e34cf882; this reviews b14882ea trial-merged with main a5d1a763 (clean merge, no conflicts, MERGEABLE).

**The earlier golden-law failure is addressed honestly.** `posted_gates/wire.rs::wire_taper_verdict` regenerates `wire_taper_punch.cl` from the generator and asserts it byte-identical to the golden, then judges it with `WireJob { taper: true }` at Z0.01, Z6 and Z11.99. It is in the `judged` list of `every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` (solid_law_goldens.rs:393), and `the_slot_trace_and_plasma_goldens_pass_their_gates` asserts it is clean and frees the part. A real gate judges it; it is not marked synthetic and main's law is not weakened (the law's own file only gains the new entry).

**Loosening check (a case refused before that now passes)**
- A pose on a cut that states no taper is still `Unreadable` (`sim/verify/wire/kerf.rs` `polyline`, `taper == false`), pinned by the "refusal of a pose on a cut with no taper" test. `WireJob.taper` is set only from `taper_deg != 0` (`wire_verify.rs`).
- Vertical wire: `reach` returns exactly `k`, so the gouge law is unchanged for every existing program; the slug law builds the same kerf at every height for a vertical wire.
- A tapered open run and a taper with a no-core burnout are refused by name (taper.rs, wire_op.rs); no side or arc path newly passes.
- No existing golden is modified: `git diff origin/main` shows only two new goldens (`wire_taper_punch.nc`, `wire_taper_punch.cl`). The zero-taper case is checked byte for byte against the existing vertical golden.
- No snapshot PNGs, no process files, no Cargo.toml or build.rs change, no new `camcraft-*` dependency.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page.rs` changes (Taper angle field); the PR body has no screenshot, noted only.
- The fixture's taper codes are invented and nothing was run on a real control (D10), as the body states.
- The wire laws sample the three judged heights; the lean is linear in height, so this is a sound basis, and the new upper-section tests pin that a gouge at one height blocks.
- Stacked on #1144 per the body; check that parent is merged or retargeted before this merges.
